ai.description: The Jammu Bent-toed Gecko reaches a snout-vent length of 45 mm. It is brownish-grey with dark crossbands and possesses strongly curved, clawed digits and granular dorsal scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtopodion mansarulum* is best distinguished by the presence of 10–12 longitudinal rows of enlarged, trihedral tubercles on its dorsum, which are absent in most congeners.
ai.habitat: The Jammu Bent-toed Gecko inhabits rocky crevices and stone walls within dry, scrub-dominated landscapes at elevations ranging from 300 to 1,000 meters in the Himalayan foothills.
ai.behavior: The Jammu bent-toed gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects on rock surfaces and walls within its arid habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtopodion mansarulum* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtopodion mansarulum* is endemic to the Jammu region of Jammu and Kashmir, India, where it is found at elevations around 400–700 meters near Mansar Lake.
